cases.notes: README §4.3 (1.1): a rebuild deletes the repo's rows and records a row only for a walked file whose bytes' hash equals its live doc's file_hash. Over an un-ingested edit the file gets no row, so the following drift still reports it `changed` and the following sweep hashes and ingests it (candidates 1, changed true). The touch afterwards is an ordinary refresh. Before 1.1 the reference recorded the disk hash of every walked file and the edit vanished (§9 "Fixed (1.1)").

cases.name: rebuild-stats-after-a-deletion-leaves-no-row
cases.notes: README §4.3: a live doc whose file is gone is not walked, so the rebuild leaves it no row and `scanned` counts only the file still on disk; drift reports it `deleted`. Pinned consequence (unchanged by 1.1): the sweep finds deletions from cache rows that are no longer on disk, so after the rebuild dropped b.md's row the following sweep has no candidate and does not tombstone it — only drift (and `recover`'s `missing`) see it.
